name_note: The GTDB genus Fusobacterium carries the same name in the literature; the work cited here concerns its species Fusobacterium nucleatum.

sentences.text: Fusobacterium nucleatum is a Gram-negative anaerobic bacterium of the normal human microbiota, originally identified in the oral cavity.
A review describes it as a ubiquitous oral commensal and a key intermediate colonizer with well-documented interspecies coaggregation activity.
That review attributes to the surface adhesins FadA and Fap2 interspecies coaggregation, support for colonization by Porphyromonas gingivalis, and epithelial barrier invasion.
Another review reports its DNA in the intratumoural microbiome of many human malignancies, and links intratumoural F. nucleatum in colorectal cancer to shorter survival across independent cohorts.
The same review notes that in oral squamous cell carcinoma F. nucleatum positivity has been linked to improved outcomes.
